extracted.intended_audience: prospective KAKENHI applicants (PIs), Co‑Investigators, research institution administrative staff, and reviewers
extracted.subtask_description: Preparation and submission procedures, eligibility rules, reviewer confidentiality and review/assessment process for JSPS Grants‑in‑Aid for Scientific Research (KAKENHI) research proposal documents. Covers PI/Co‑I responsibilities, electronic submission, parallel‑grant restrictions, and items that cause outright rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer confidentiality obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers must maintain confidentiality of Research Proposal Documents and information learned during review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To protect applicants' intellectual property and ensure fairness, reviewers must not disclose proposal content or related information to outside parties (including superiors, colleagues, subordinates), must not use information learned in the review for their own benefit, and must keep review materials under strict control.

rubrics_metrics.name: Composition and methods of comprehensive review
rubrics_metrics.description: Review is conducted as Document Review and Panel Review by three Section‑specific Committees (humanities/social sciences; science/engineering; biological sciences).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document Review is performed by about 8–14 reviewers in each committee and uses the Research Proposal Document, Review Comments, and Overseas Reviews (about three domestic comment authors and about three overseas reviewers). Extremely low marks in overseas reviews can lead to non-adoption. Preliminary Screening may precede Document Review; Panel Review discusses proposals broadly and selects projects for interview reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of external databases in review
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers may utilize researchmap and the Grants‑in‑Aid Database (KAKEN) as necessary during review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers can consult registered researcher information and KAKEN entries to assist assessment; applicants are instructed to register researcher information in researchmap as part of preparation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification of review results
rubrics_metrics.description: JSPS notifies applicants and institutions of various review outcomes via the electronic application system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notifications include preliminary screening results for non‑adopted proposals, selection for interviews, final adoption decisions, opinions expressed in reviews for adopted projects, approximate ranks within sections for non‑adopted proposals, and release of summary opinions for adopted projects on KAKEN and other media.

rubrics_metrics.name: PI eligibility at submission
rubrics_metrics.description: At submission, a PI must be approved by their research institution as eligible and be registered in e‑Rad as eligible for KAKENHI application, meeting three requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The three requirements: (1) belong to a research institution with a job assignment that includes research activity (paid/unpaid, full/part‑time irrelevant), (2) actually be engaged in research activity (not merely research assisting jobs), and (3) not be a graduate student or other student (exceptions if one holds a position with research as main job and also holds student status). The applying PI must obtain institutional approval that the project is authorized by the institution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research institution responsibilities and eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: The research institution must authorize the project as proper activity and take responsibility for KAKENHI management and accounting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The institution must be one designated under the Rules for the Handling of Grants‑in‑Aid and must verify PI/Co‑I eligibility at submission. Institutions can withhold submission if they judge it inappropriate to let an individual conduct the research as part of institutional work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ineligibility due to prior misconduct or penalties
rubrics_metrics.description: Individuals penalized for improper grant spending, fraudulent acquisition, or research misconduct may be ineligible to apply or have eligibility suspended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If registered as ineligible for grant acquisition in the fiscal year (penalty), the individual cannot apply. Failure to submit post‑project 'Report on the Research Achievements' without good reason can result in suspension or withholding of future grant delivery.

rubrics_metrics.name: KAKENHI employee restrictions on applying
rubrics_metrics.description: Researchers employed with a KAKENHI grant (KAKENHI employees) are generally bound to employment‑related work and cannot apply for their own KAKENHI project carried out during those working hours unless conditions are met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conditions allowing application: employment contract explicitly grants conducting self‑initiated research besides employment work; clear demarcation of employment‑related work and own research hours/effort; securing enough research hours outside employment work to perform the KAKENHI project. These must be verified by the research institution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Self‑motivated research by young KAKENHI employees
rubrics_metrics.description: Young researchers employed with KAKENHI may conduct their own research during employment hours under specified conditions and may apply as PI or Co‑I.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conditions: (1) the young researcher desires to conduct own research; (2) PI and Co‑I (employer) deem the research positively contributes to funded project and institution approves; (3) PI/Co‑I judge the effort spared will not hinder funded project and institution approves. Upper limit of effort spared is 20% of efforts devoted to the funded project. 'Young researcher' defined as age 39 or under or less than 8 years after PhD (excluding certain parental leave periods) as of April 1 of fiscal year. If funding resources change, reapproval is necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: JSPS Fellows (SPD/PD/RPD/CPD/DC) application rules
rubrics_metrics.description: JSPS Research Fellows have specific allowances and restrictions for KAKENHI applications depending on fellowship type.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: JSPS Fellows (except DC) who meet application requirements at their host institution may apply for many research categories as Co‑I and some as PI; Fellows (DC) are deemed eligible by nomination for certain categories but can apply as PI only for Grant‑in‑Aid for JSPS Fellows and Fostering Joint International Research, and may participate as Co‑Is only from host institution. Host institutions should avoid overburdening Fellows (DC) with excessive responsibilities. Researcher Number required for certain parallel applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on student applicants
rubrics_metrics.description: Students (e.g., graduate students) and International Research Fellows cannot apply for KAKENHI grants, with specific exceptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exception: an individual who holds a position in a research institution with research as main job and simultaneously holds student status is eligible. Institutions should check definitions and eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: e‑Rad registration confirmation requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Researchers must confirm proper registration of Researcher Information in e‑Rad before submitting the Research Proposal Document.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registration is handled by the research institution; researchers should check with their administrative section about registration deadlines, confirmation methods, and update entries (e.g., affiliation, position) if needed. An ID/password is issued after registration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic application system access and credential handling
rubrics_metrics.description: An e‑Rad ID and password are required to access the KAKENHI Electronic Application System; researchers must handle credentials carefully.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ID/password remains valid after moving institutions. Researchers must prevent leakage and abuse. Use the Electronic Application System to prepare and upload Research Proposal Document PDF files.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on parallel grant application/receipt — principles
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules limiting parallel submission and receipt of grants aim to distribute limited funding fairly and avoid overburdening review processes and PIs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Basic principles: (①) support as many excellent researchers as possible, (②) avoid excessive number of applications relative to review capacity, (③) restrictions primarily target PIs (may extend to Co‑Is for large budgets), (④) restrictions on submission and simultaneous receipt are set per category considering purpose and characteristics. Applicants should avoid 'unreasonable duplication' per related guidelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific restriction for International Leading Research
rubrics_metrics.description: You can propose or receive no more than one International Leading Research project at the same time, as PI or Co‑I.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A PI or Co‑I of a prospective ongoing project in FY2024 cannot submit a new proposal in this research category. Violations may lead to elimination from review even after submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Important considerations about parallel applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants should check restrictions before submission and consider workload and responsibility even when not prohibited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if parallel submission is allowed, submitting many projects may prevent fulfilling PI/Co‑I responsibilities. All applied projects involving the same researcher may not be reviewed. There is no restriction between KAKENHI and other funding schemes, but applicants must be mindful of policies on elimination of duplication and overconcentration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality and research ethics in Research Proposal Document
rubrics_metrics.description: Research Proposal Document contents must be original and prepared in compliance with research ethics; plagiarism and misappropriation are strictly impermissible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The entire document, including the title, will be reviewed and publicized if adopted. Choose a title that effectively reflects project content since adopted projects are widely publicized in the KAKEN database.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structure and required components of Research Proposal Document
rubrics_metrics.description: The Research Proposal Document consists of 'Items to be entered in the Website' and 'Forms to be uploaded'; submission must be PDF via the Electronic Application System.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare items on the electronic system (title, budget, project members, expenditure) and upload prescribed forms downloaded from JSPS. Paper applications are not accepted. The PI must submit the completed PDF to their institution's administrative section by the institution's deadline; direct submission to JSPS is not allowed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Letter of Intent (LOI) requirements for overseas joint researchers
rubrics_metrics.description: Letters of Intent from overseas joint researchers must be collected and uploaded as part of the Research Proposal Document using Form S‑64(L).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: LOIs confirm the overseas researcher jointly conducts the project; ask leading researcher(s) to complete and sign. Save related correspondence (emails). If received on paper, convert to PDF before upload. If multiple overseas joint researchers are involved, select up to three leading researchers for LOI submission. Uploaded LOIs will be used in review and personal information contained will be used for administrative tasks (may be provided to external contractors).

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic submission procedures and deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must complete preparation and upload of the Research Proposal Document via the Electronic Application System and submit the document to their institution's administrative section by the institution's deadline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After preparing PDFs and entering website items, complete the 'Check Completed and Submission' stage to submit to the institution. No corrections or modifications are possible after the institution's submission deadline. Personal information in proposals will be used for administrative purposes and may be made public for adopted projects per law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personal information handling and public disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Personal information in proposals and the electronic system will be used for administrative tasks and may be provided to contractors, e‑Rad, and governmental offices; adopted project information is 'planned to be made public.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Information may be supplied to the Cabinet Office via e‑Rad and used for policy questionnaires. Applicants should understand information handling (utilization, provision, disclosure) and may be asked to cooperate in verification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Important checkpoints to avoid outright rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain types of research plans are outside KAKENHI funding scope and risk outright rejection by incompleteness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plans outside scope include: A) merely purchasing ready‑made research equipment; B) building large‑size research facilities/equipment better funded elsewhere; C) developing/selling goods or services (including associated market research); D) entrusted research conducted as regular business; E) plans with yearly budget < ¥100,000. Applicants should ensure their plan does not fall into these categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility and composition of project members (team design)
rubrics_metrics.description: PIs must organize a research team with an appropriate combination of Co‑Investigators and Research Collaborators to achieve objectives, considering diversity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify KAKENHI eligibility of PI and Co‑Is by their institutions at proposal submission. Research Collaborators do not need e‑Rad registration. The PI is the main recipient bearing full responsibility (including summarization of achievements); individuals likely to lose eligibility during the research period should refrain from PI/Co‑I roles; substitutions of PI generally not permitted (exception: International Leading Research with procedures).

rubrics_metrics.name: Principal Investigator responsibilities and requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The PI bears full responsibility for implementation of the research project and must ensure Co‑I consent and eligibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PI must obtain consent from Co‑Investigators via the electronic application system before submitting the Research Proposal Document to the institution, be registered in e‑Rad as 'Eligible for KAKENHI Application', and not be designated as 'ineligible for grant receipt' in the relevant fiscal year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Co‑Investigator responsibilities and requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Co‑Investigators share responsibility with the PI according to clearly defined roles and must be recipients of a share of the grant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A Co‑I must be registered in e‑Rad as 'Eligible for KAKENHI Application' and not be designated as 'ineligible for grant receipt' in the fiscal year. Individuals who are likely to lose eligibility during the research period should refrain from becoming Co‑Is.

rubrics_metrics.name: Co‑Investigator participation process (consent via system)
rubrics_metrics.description: Adding a Co‑Investigator requires an electronic consent process through the application system with actions by both PI and Co‑I.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PI must enter the researcher information in the 'Project Members List' on the Application Information Input screen, request the researcher to become a Co‑Investigator, and obtain their consent by the time of submitting the Research Proposal Document to the research institution. The consent process is conducted via the electronic application system; Co‑Is must complete required steps in the system.
